title: Current Electricity — 40 MCQs
description: Covers Ohm’s law, electrical resistance, resistivity and conductivity, R = ρl/A, sensors (strain gauge, LDR, thermistor), ohmic and non-ohmic behaviour, series and parallel combinations, potential divider, e.m.f. and internal resistance, electrical power, and the microscopic expression for current.

questions.q: Ohm’s law states that the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference across it provided
questions.explanation: Ohm’s law holds only when physical conditions, especially temperature, are kept constant.

questions.q: Electric resistance is defined as the ratio of
questions.explanation: R = V / I by definition.

questions.q: The SI unit of resistance is
questions.explanation: One ohm is the resistance of a conductor when 1 V produces a current of 1 A.

questions.q: Resistivity ρ of a material is given by
questions.explanation: From R = ρ l / A it follows that ρ = R A / l.

The resistance of a wire is doubled when its
options: both length and area are doubled
questions.explanation: R ∝ l when A is constant, so doubling length doubles resistance.

questions.q: In a series combination of resistors the total resistance is
options: equal to the sum of the individual resistances
equal to the reciprocal of the sum of reciprocals
questions.explanation: R_s = R₁ + R₂ + … for series connection.

questions.q: The e.m.f. of a cell is the energy transferred by the cell in driving
options: unit charge round a complete circuit
unit charge through the external circuit only
all the charge through the internal resistance
questions.explanation: e.m.f. is defined as the work done per unit charge by the source in a complete circuit.

questions.q: Power dissipated in a resistor R carrying current I is
questions.explanation: P = I² R (also equal to V I and V² / R).

questions.q: Electric current is defined as the rate of flow of
questions.explanation: By convention current is the rate of flow of positive charge: I = dQ/dt.

A metallic conductor at constant temperature has an I–V graph that is
options: a straight line through the origin
a curve concave to the V-axis
a curve concave to the I-axis
questions.explanation: Ohmic conductors obey V ∝ I, giving a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: The I–V characteristic of a filament lamp is non-ohmic because
questions.explanation: As the filament heats, its resistance rises, so the graph curves and does not remain linear.

questions.q: A potential divider consists of two resistors 2 kΩ and 3 kΩ in series across a 10 V supply. The p.d. across the 3 kΩ resistor is
questions.explanation: Voltage division: V = 10 × (3/(2+3)) = 6 V.

questions.q: A cell of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 0.5 Ω is connected to a 2.5 Ω resistor. The terminal p.d. is
The resistance of an n-type thermistor
questions.explanation: In an n-type thermistor the number of charge carriers increases with temperature, lowering the resistance.

questions.q: The resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR)
options: increases with increase in light intensity
decreases with increase in light intensity
questions.explanation: Higher light intensity generates more charge carriers, reducing the resistance of the LDR.

questions.q: A strain gauge works on the principle that resistance changes with
options: change in dimensions caused by strain
questions.explanation: Strain alters the length and cross-sectional area of the gauge wire, changing its resistance according to R = ρ l / A.

questions.q: Three resistors of 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance is
A wire of resistance 10 Ω is stretched to twice its original length. Assuming volume is constant its new resistance is
questions.explanation: Volume constant ⇒ A' = A/2; R' = ρ (2l)/(A/2) = 4 (ρ l / A) = 40 Ω.

questions.q: The power delivered by a 12 V battery that supplies a current of 2 A is
Two identical cells each of e.m.f. 1.5 V and internal resistance 1 Ω are connected in series to an external resistance of 4 Ω. The current in the circuit is
questions.explanation: Total E = 3 V, total r = 2 Ω; I = 3/(4+2) = 0.5 A.

questions.q: The microscopic expression for current is I = n A v q. Here n stands for
options: number of free charge carriers per unit volume
questions.explanation: n is the number density of free charge carriers.

questions.q: A semiconductor diode is a non-ohmic device because its I–V graph is
options: a straight line through the origin
not a straight line through the origin
questions.explanation: A diode conducts appreciably only in one direction and its characteristic is highly non-linear.

questions.q: A copper wire of length 1 m and area 1 mm² has resistivity 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. Its resistance is
Four resistors of 4 Ω each are connected to form a square. The resistance between two adjacent corners is
questions.explanation: Between adjacent corners one resistor is in parallel with the series combination of the other three: R = 4 ∥ 12 = 3 Ω.

questions.explanation: Total external R = 4 Ω; I = 2/(4+0.5) = 0.4 A; V = I R = 0.4 × 4 = 1.6 V.

questions.explanation: Thermistor resistance falls with rising temperature, so the p.d. across it decreases if it forms the lower part of the divider.

questions.explanation: Parallel of 4 Ω and 4 Ω = 2 Ω; then series with 2 Ω gives 4 Ω.

When a 12 V battery of internal resistance 0.5 Ω is short-circuited the current is
questions.explanation: Short-circuit current = E / r = 12 / 0.5 = 24 A.

questions.q: The equivalent resistance between points A and B of a network consisting of three 6 Ω resistors forming a triangle is
questions.explanation: Two resistors in series (12 Ω) are in parallel with the third (6 Ω): R = (12 × 6)/(12+6) = 4 Ω.

options: as the upper resistor of the divider
as the lower resistor of the divider
in parallel with the fixed resistor
